justification_text:
My point estimates across all three horizons reflect a relatively stable near-term outlook with modest upward drift. At the one-day horizon, the estimate of 1,136 was anchored primarily to the prevailing spot price or last observed level, with only a small expected move given typical daily volatility in the underlying asset. For the one-week estimate of 1,140, I incorporated a slight continuation of recent momentum while acknowledging mean-reverting tendencies that prevent large directional bets over short windows. The one-month estimate of 1,150 reflects a similarly muted drift assumption, essentially projecting that the fundamental backdrop remains broadly unchanged and that no major structural shift occurs over the coming weeks.

The confidence interval widths expand in a way that mirrors how uncertainty compounds over time. At one day, the 90% interval of roughly plus or minus 31 points reflects normal intraday and overnight volatility. By one week, that band widens to about plus or minus 55 points as day-to-day fluctuations accumulate and the probability of encountering an unexpected macro data release or policy signal increases. At one month, the interval stretches to plus or minus 120 points, capturing the realistic possibility of several meaningful events — earnings, central bank decisions, or geopolitical developments — that could shift sentiment materially in either direction. The widening also accounts for the fact that short-term mean reversion is less of a stabilizing force over longer horizons.

Several specific risks could push outcomes well outside these stated intervals. On the downside, a sharper-than-expected tightening of financial conditions, a significant negative data surprise such as a recession signal or a credit event, or an escalation in geopolitical tensions could drive prices meaningfully below the lower bound of the one-month interval. On the upside, a dovish policy pivot, stronger-than-expected growth data, or a relief rally following the resolution of an ongoing uncertainty could push prices above 1,270. Liquidity conditions also matter — thin markets during holiday periods or around major scheduled events can amplify moves in ways that standard volatility estimates understate. These tail scenarios are real possibilities even if they fall outside the 90% range by construction.
